simple.meaning: דָּמַם (dâmam) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be dumb ; by implication, to be astonished , to stop ; also to perish.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 30 times across Exodus, Leviticus, Joshua, 1 Samuel, Job, and 6 more, beginning at Exodus 15:16. Its contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דָּמַם (H1826).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: דָּמַם (dâmam) / H1826 is traced through Exodus 15:16, Leviticus 10:3, Joshua 10:12, Joshua 10:13 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to be dumb ; by implication, to be astonished , to stop ; also to perish
definitions.usage: cease, be cut down (off), forbear, hold peace, quiet self, rest, be silent, keep (put to) silence, be (stand) still, tarry, wait.
definitions.full: H1826. damam I. [ דָּמַם ] verb be or grow dumb, silent, still (Late Hebrew id. ; Ethiopic in II. stupefy ; III., 1 & 2 be astounded, stupefied ) — Qal Perfect דַּ֫מּוּ Job 30:27 , דָּ֑מּוּ Psa 35:15 ; Imperfect יִדֹּם Amos 5:13 2 t., וַיִּדֹּם Lev 10:3 ; Josh 10:13 ; 3 feminine singular תִּדֹּם Lam 2:18 ; 2 feminine singular תִּדֹּמִּי Jer 48:2 (so Ki Ol & Kö 327 q. v.; others Niph`al); וָאֶדֹּם Job 31:34 : יִדְּמוּ Exod 15:16 3 t.; 1 plural cohortative נִדְּמָה Jer 8:14 (so Thes Ol Bö Kö 327q. see; others Niph`al); — 1 be silent Psa 4:5 ; Psalm 30:13; 35:15 (probably, compare De Che), Ezek 24:17 ; Lev 10:3 (P) Amos 5:13 ; in grief Lam 2:10 ; 3:28 . 2 be still (opposed to both speech and motion) Job 31:34 ; = perish Jer 8:14 ; 48:2 ; Psa 31:18 ( ׳ד לשׁאול ); with לְ be silent to i.e. be resigned to 37:7 ; 62:6 , followed by עֲצָתִי לְמוֺ Job 29:21 (|| שָֽׁמְעוּ לִי ); be still , motionless, stand still Josh 10:12-13 , (of sun || עמד ); 1Sam 14:9 (men); Jer 47:6 (of sword || הֵרָֽגְעִי ); so also of bowels, as seat of mental excitement Job 30:27 ; Lam 2:18 בַּתעֵֿינֵךְ אַלתִּֿדֹּם , i.e. cease not to weep (|| דִּמְעָה כַנַּחַל הוֺרִידִי ). 3 be struck dumb, astounded , in amazement and fear Exod 15:16 ( כאבן ) Isa 23:2 (but compare II. דמם ). Niph`al Perfect 3plural וְנָדַמּוּ consecutive Jer 25:37 ; Imperfect יִדַּמּוּ 49:26 ; 50:30 , יִדָּ֑מּוּ 1Sam 2:9 ; 2 masculine plural תִּדַּמּוּ Jer 51:6 — be made silent , i.e. destroyed; the wicked 1Sam 2:9 ( בַּחשֶׁךְ ), compare Jer 51:6 ; men of war 49:25 ; 50:30 ; dwellings 25:37 . Po. Perfect 1singular נַפְשִׁי וְדוֺמַ֫מְתִּי שִׁוִּיתִי Psa 131:2 ' composed and quieted my soul Che (as a weaned child). Hiph`il Perfect 3masculine singular suffix הֲדִמָּנוּ he (God) hath silenced us ( = caused to perish) Jer 8:14 . II. [ דָּמַם ] verb wail (?; compare Assyrian damâmu , groan, wail , lament , Dl Baer's Ezech xi; pr 64 ) — only Qal Imperative אִי ישְׁבֵי דֹּ֫מּוּ Isa 23:2 wail, ye coast dwellers (compare Dl l.c .), || הֵילִילוּ 23:1 , & אִי ישְׁבֵי הֵילִילוּ 23:6 ; most, however, assign this to I. דמם q. v. occurrences.englishText: Terror and dread falls on them.
Then Moses said to Aaron, “This is what Yahweh spoke of, saying,

Then Joshua spoke to Yahweh in the day when Yahweh delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel. He said in the sight of Israel, “Sun, stand still on Gibeon! You, moon, stop in the valley of Aijalon!”

The sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies. Isn’t this written in the book of Jashar? The sun stayed in the middle of the sky, and didn’t hurry to go down about a whole day.
He will keep the feet of his holy ones,
If they say this to us, ‘Wait until we come to you!’ then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up to them.
“Men listened to me, waited,
My heart is troubled, and doesn’t rest.
because I feared the great multitude,
Offer the sacrifices of righteousness.
Let the lying lips be mute,
But in my adversity, they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together.
Rest in Yahweh, and wait patiently for him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress.
Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul,
Be still, you inhabitants of the coast, you whom the merchants of Sidon that pass over the sea, have replenished.
“Why do we sit still?
“Why do we sit still?
The peaceful folds are brought to silence
“ ‘You sword of Yahweh, how long will it be before you are quiet?
The praise of Moab is no more.
Therefore her young men will fall in her streets,
Therefore her young men will fall in her streets.
“Flee out of the middle of Babylon!
The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground.
Their heart cried to the Lord.
Let him sit alone and keep silence,
Sigh, but not aloud. Make no mourning for the dead. Bind your headdress on you, and put your sandals on your feet. Don’t cover your lips, and don’t eat mourner’s bread.”
Therefore a prudent person keeps silent in such a time,
